title: Weekly Dose of Optimism #212
gist: Packy McCormick's roundup highlights five frontier-tech signals: Vironexis' in-vivo AAV gene therapy VNX-101 turning liver cells into a factory for a CD19xCD3 bispecific (3/3 complete responses in a small ALL subgroup); Solcoa's $75M raise to scale US rare-earth metallization 50x in Nevada as a link in an emerging Western mine-to-motor chain; Terraform producing high-purity methanol from sunlight and air; Joby's 3,199-mile autonomous cross-country flight; and Meta's 100-gram, $1,299.99 VR Glasses as evidence Zuckerberg's long-term glasses convergence plan is on track.

insights.claim: Vironexis reported that all three patients in a subgroup with relapsed or refractory acute lymphoblastic leukemia achieved complete responses with no residual leukemia detected after a single administration of its AAV gene therapy VNX-101; the first patient's response lasted 260 days before proceeding to stem cell transplant.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Early efficacy signal for one-shot in-vivo bispecific therapy in blood cancers; worth tracking Vironexis' broader Phase 1/2 readouts before extrapolating from n=3.
insights.quote: all three patients in a subgroup with relapsed or refractory acute lymphoblastic leukemia achieved complete responses after a single administration of VNX-101
insights.locator: (1) Vironexis Turns the Liver Into a Cancer Drug Factory

insights.claim: VNX-101 uses an adeno-associated virus to deliver genetic instructions to liver cells, which then continuously produce GP101, a protein that binds CD19 on cancer cells and CD3 on T cells, bridging killer T cells to their targets without repeated dosing.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Combines gene therapy delivery with bispecific T-cell engager biology — a platform approach that could threaten recurring-infusion bispecific franchises if durable and safe.
insights.quote: like a little pharmaceutical factory manufacturing the treatment inside the body

insights.claim: The Vironexis results carry heavy caveats: the responding patients had no pre-existing anti-AAV antibodies, the broader Phase 1/2 trial has treated only nine people across several blood cancers, results are early and company-reported, and cytokine release syndrome and neurological toxicity occurred during dose escalation (resolved with treatment).
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Pre-existing anti-AAV antibody exclusion limits addressable population; CRS/neurotoxicity and durability are the key diligence items for in-vivo bispecific programs.

insights.claim: If patients' own cells can safely take over drug manufacturing, a large share of the pharma industry's effort and cost spent on manufacturing medicines and repeatedly administering them could be displaced, reducing infusion time for patients.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Second-order risk to biologics CDMOs and infusion-center economics if in-vivo production platforms mature.

insights.claim: Solcoa raised $75 million — $45 million equity led by Bain Capital Ventures and $30 million debt and equipment financing anchored by J.P. Morgan — to build Solcoa One, a Nevada rare-earth metalmaking plant designed for 500 tonnes a year, targeting operations in July 2027.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Bank debt anchoring an early-stage rare-earth processing plant signals financeability of US critical-minerals midstream; July 2027 is the milestone to watch.
insights.locator: (2) Solcoa Raises $75M for American Rare Earth Metallization

insights.claim: Solcoa currently produces neodymium-praseodymium and samarium metal at about 10 tonnes a year in Alameda, a negligible amount against a roughly 100-kiloton-per-year NdPr market and 2-kiloton-per-year samarium market; the new plant would scale it 50x, with a hoped-for further 6x afterward.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Even at 500 t/yr, US metallization would be well under 1% of the NdPr market — sizing context for how far Western supply is from displacing China.
insights.quote: 10 tonnes doesn’t do much against a 100-kiloton-a-year NdPr market and a 2 kiloton-a-year samarium market

insights.claim: Solcoa's metallization process — converting refined rare earth oxides into metals usable by magnet makers — combines new chemistry with self-built modular reactors and is claimed to use less energy and cost less than conventional molten-salt electrolysis.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Process-technology differentiation, not just subsidy, is the potential cost edge for Western rare-earth processors; validate claims against unit economics at scale.

insights.claim: China currently dominates the rare-earth supply chain, and developing new technology rather than copying incumbent processes is the key way the United States will catch up.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Favors backing novel-process rare-earth startups over conventional-process capacity when positioning for supply-chain decoupling.
insights.quote: Developing new technology is the key way America will catch up to China.

insights.claim: A Western rare-earth supply chain is visibly forming across discrete startups: Earth AI for exploration, Solcoa for metallization, Vulcan Elements for magnets (now supplying brushless drone motors for the Army's SkyFoundry drone initiative, per Axios, after a $1.4 billion partnership with the government and ReElement), and Westmag for motors and actuators for drones and robots.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Map of investable nodes in the Western mine-to-magnet-to-motor stack; defense drone demand (SkyFoundry) is an anchor offtaker de-risking magnet producers.
insights.quote: Earth AI can find them. Solcoa can metallize them. Vulcan can turn them into magnets.
insights.locator: (2) Solcoa — Vulcan and the western chain

insights.claim: Terraform Industries produced batches of high-purity methanol at its Muroc desert test site, following a fast 2026 build-out: site closed in January, construction by March, 1.8 MW of solar installed by May, on-site CO2 in July and hydrogen in August.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Execution cadence of roughly one new molecule every couple of months is the key signal for synthetic-fuel startups; cost at scale remains unproven.
insights.locator: (3) Terraform Makes Methanol From Sunlight and Air

insights.claim: Methanol gives Terraform, which already makes and sells methane, a second route into replacing oil-and-gas-derived products, since methanol is a feedstock for gasoline, aviation fuel and plastics.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Solar-to-methanol widens the addressable petrochemical substitution market beyond natural gas — long-dated competitive threat to fossil feedstock chains if costs fall.

insights.claim: Terraform's go-to-market strategy is to first sell high-purity products that command premium prices, then use production experience to drive costs down until it can compete in larger, cheaper commodity markets; the open question is what cost it can reach at scale.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Classic learning-curve beachhead strategy — monitor Terraform's realized cost per unit versus commodity methanol/methane benchmarks as the proof point.
insights.quote: start with high-purity products that command higher prices

insights.claim: Joby's J208, a converted Cessna Caravan rather than one of its electric air taxis, flew 3,199 miles across the United States with zero control inputs from the onboard safety pilot, handling taxi, takeoff, navigation and landing, busy airports and severe-weather rerouting, with stops in Arizona, Texas and South Carolina before ending near Kitty Hawk.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Demonstrates Joby's autonomy stack is maturing independently of its eVTOL certification path — potential optionality in autonomous cargo/conventional aircraft.
insights.quote: flown 3,199 miles across the United States with zero control inputs from the onboard safety pilot

insights.claim: Autonomy across boats, drones, robotaxis and aircraft will reshape how people and goods move, but the author frames autonomy itself as just table stakes — only one piece of a larger puzzle he promises to elaborate on next week.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: If autonomy commoditizes, value capture shifts to whatever complements it (vehicles, networks, energy) — avoid paying a premium for autonomy alone.
insights.quote: But autonomy is just one piece of the puzzle, table stakes.

themes.theme: Meta Connect and the glasses convergence bet

insights.claim: At Meta Connect, Meta unveiled Meta VR Glasses — a 100-gram VR headset with a 5K micro-OLED display, eye and hand controls, and the ability to turn flat surfaces into a keyboard and touchpad — due spring 2027 at $1,299.99 with up to three hours of media playback, plus 100+ immersive live US sporting events a year, 3D movies and hologram calling.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Sub-$1,300, 100g form factor is a meaningful step toward mass-market headsets; spring 2027 launch and sports-content deals are the adoption catalysts to watch.

insights.claim: Meta also gave its Muse AI assistant voice and video, enabled Meta Glasses to act as FDA-approved hearing aids, launched audio-only glasses and a keychain Muse Charm device — all aimed at pulling users away from the Apple iPhone.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Meta is attacking iPhone's role as the default AI interface via multiple wearable form factors; FDA hearing-aid clearance opens a health-adjacent market for smart glasses.
insights.quote: Anything to get you away from your Apple iPhone.

insights.claim: Despite heavy criticism of the tens of billions Zuckerberg spent on the Metaverse, the author argues his long-stated plan — lightweight everyday glasses (Meta Ray-Bans) and bulkier AR/VR devices converging over time into one comfortable, stylish pair more capable than today's best headsets — is on track and he will ultimately be proven right.
insights.speaker: Packy McCormick
insights.so_what: Contrarian bull case on Meta's Reality Labs spend: treat it as a converging-hardware roadmap rather than sunk cost, with each device launch a checkpoint.
insights.quote: More importantly, they’re a sign that the plan is on track, and that ultimately, Zuck is going to be right.
